reason: The passage depicts Moses acting unilaterally and without authorization or support from the Hebrew people. When Moses intervenes in a dispute between two Hebrew men, one directly challenges his authority, asking 'Who made you a leader and judge over us?' (מִי שָׂמְךָ לְאִישׁ שַׂר וְשֹׁפֵט עָלֵינוּ). This explicit question demonstrates a fundamental lack of recognition of his leadership and absence of collaboration. The passage shows conflict and rejection rather than cooperation, culminating in Pharaoh seeking to kill Moses, forcing him to flee. There is no evidence of leaders and people working together; instead, the text shows opposition and disconnection.
